variant: Anderson-Greenwood / Bellanca T-250 Aries = FAA Model 51 (TCDS A11SW, approved 28 Jul 1976; Lycoming O-540-A4D5 carbureted 250 hp). The Model 51A (IO-540-C4B5 fuel-injected, approved 16 Jun 1980) shares the TC; no separate 51A geometry or performance was found. Wikipedia also lists an 'AG-250' designation (Air Progress Nov 1978). The geometry is the published Jane's/AOPA brochure data for the production-standard airplane; the AOPA flight test was done on prototype N51AG (s/n 0001).
config: tractor, low wing, T-tail with all-moving stabilator, retractable tricycle gear, single engine

span.note: 31 ft 4 in, AOPA Pilot Mar 1977 spec table (manufacturer data); same in Jane's 1980-81 via Wikipedia. Aerofiles gives 31 ft 9 in (unexplained).

area.note: AOPA spec table; Jane's 1980-81 via Wikipedia. Wing loading 18.5 lb/sq ft at 3150 lb. AR = 5.77 (computed by us).

root_chord.note: E (ours): area/span = 170/31.33 ft = 5.43 ft. Plane & Pilot describes the wings and T-tail as laminar-flow constant-chord, so we took root = tip = mean chord. This assumes the area includes the fuselage carry-through; no measured chord was found.

tip_chord.note: E (ours): same as root (constant chord per Plane & Pilot).

sweep_le_deg.note: E (ours): implied by the constant-chord rectangular planform; not published.

wing.airfoil: NACA "60-412" per Lednicer's Incomplete Guide to Airfoil Usage (quotation marks are the guide's) [B, https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/ads/aircraft.html]; Wikipedia (citing Jane's 1980-81) gives 'NACA 600412 modified' [F]. Both describe a 6-series laminar section, 12% thick. AOPA 1977 and Plane & Pilot call it a laminar-flow wing. Exact designation unresolved.

tc_root.note: from the '412' in the designation; not independently confirmed

canard_or_htail.airfoil: laminar-flow constant-chord section per Plane & Pilot (designation not given). T-tail stabilator with tab; travel TE up 15 deg / down 2 deg; trim range up 7 deg / down 0.25 deg with tab faired (TCDS A11SW).

vtail.note: Single swept fin carrying the T-tail stabilator. Rudder travel 30 deg each way (TCDS). Overall height 8 ft 7 in (AOPA spec table). AOPA 1977 flight test: a rudder input in smooth air gave considerable back-and-forth rebounding of the tail before the yaw damped out (weak yaw damping).

length.note: 26 ft 2 in overall (AOPA spec table; Jane's via Wikipedia). Aerofiles 26 ft 7 in.

cabin_width.note: AOPA spec table; cabin length 115 in, cabin height 48.5 in

fuselage.note: Slab-sided, nearly flat-bellied aluminum fuselage, deliberately built from flat skins and simple (not compound) curves to cut production cost (Plane & Pilot 2010; Wikipedia). Flush riveting, butt-jointed skins, flush vents/drains/breather, sealed nose-gear doors (Plane & Pilot). One car-style cabin door. Seats: 4, or 5 with the optional fifth seat at station +182 (TCDS Note 3). Baggage 250 lb at +174.

gear: retractable tricycle. Mains retract inward and stow under the rear seat behind flush gear doors, which allows a thinner wing but gives a narrow track (about car width) and sluggish ground steering (AOPA 1977). Nose wheel steerable 30 deg each way (TCDS). Max gear operating/extended speed 166 mph CAS / 144 kt (TCDS); AOPA quotes 168 mph. Emergency hand crank between the rear seats.
cooling: air; single inlet below the spinner (Plane & Pilot 2024); no cowl flaps (AOPA 1977)

diameter.note: Hartzell HC-E2YR-1BF/F8465-7R or HC-E2YR-1S/8465-7R, 76-77 in; AOPA spec table 77 in

rpm_cruise.note: rpm at the AOPA 6,500 ft cruise point (22.5 inHg full throttle). TCDS placard: do not exceed 27 inHg below 2300 rpm.

engine.model: Lycoming O-540-A4D5, carbureted, 2,000 h TBO (Model 51); Lycoming IO-540-C4B5 with Bendix RSA-5AD1 injector (Model 51A). Owner sites list IO-540-B4C5 for N77CT; the FAA registry engine code for N77CT/N250DJ/N250MG is the Lycoming O-540 series, and for s/n 0001 (N251AG) the IO-540 series.

empty.note: AOPA spec table 'Empty weight (dry)'; useful load 1,300 lb. Plane & Pilot 2010 gives 1,888 lb (useful 1,262).

fuel_usable.note: 80 gal total in 2 wing tanks at +117; 76 usable

perf_points.power_pct_or_hp: 73% (calculated by AOPA): 22.5 inHg full throttle / 2300 rpm
perf_points.note: AOPA Pilot flight check of prototype N51AG, Mar 1977: 185 mph IAS, 208 mph TAS at OAT 50 F; aircraft 'partially loaded' (weight not stated). Converted from mph by us.

perf_points.power_pct_or_hp: full throttle, prop full forward (2575 rpm, ~100%)
perf_points.note: AOPA: 215 mph indicated, 217 mph true, choppy air. Converted from mph by us.
Manufacturer 'Normal cruise speed (75% power)' 208 mph, AOPA spec table; altitude not stated. Plane & Pilot 2010 also gives 208 mph.
Manufacturer 'Economy cruise speed (65% power)' 200 mph; altitude not stated. Jane's 1980-81 via Wikipedia: 200 mph at 65%.
Jane's 1980-81 via Wikipedia: 215 mph at sea level; AOPA spec table 215 mph (altitude not stated). Aerofiles: 216 mph top / 201 mph cruise.
Published stall 72 mph clean / 64 mph gear and flaps down; AOPA measured 69 / 63 mph (IAS). Climb 1,240 fpm; ceiling 18,100 ft.

range_points.basis: normal cruise 75%, 45-min reserve, 76 gal usable; altitude not stated
economy cruise with 45-min reserve. The AOPA table labels this '55% power' while its economy-speed line says 65%, so the power setting is ambiguous. Wikipedia/Jane's: 1,170 mi 'with four passengers'.

fleet_size_for_rate.note: FAA registry (ReleasableAircraft.zip, downloaded 2026-10-24), all status V. Model code 1225051 (BELLANCA AIRCRAFT CORP. model 51): N250DJ s/n 0003-80 (CA), N77CT s/n 0004-80 (TX), N250MG s/n 0005-80 (TX), all standard normal. Model code 0740151 (ANDERSON GREENWOOD model 51): N251AG s/n 0001 (1976, TX, certification code 40 = experimental), i.e. the prototype ex-N51AG. DEREG: N250BB s/n 0007-80 and N250DD s/n 0006-80, cancelled 2010/2011; last action 1980-03-15, never with an owner name, so probably never completed (also suggested in the archived 2004 owner page). Note: ACFTREF code 0740102 'AND-51-A' covers 1950s serials 1-5 (N3900K etc.) that are AG-14s, not Aries; excluded. Number built: Wikipedia 5; Plane & Pilot 2024 four customer airplanes plus one structural-test airframe; TCDS eligibility s/n 0001, 0003 and up.

safety.pattern: RECORD: one NTSB event in about 50 years: a ground loss of control while taxiing, with a main gear collapse and no injuries (1983). Fleet exposure is tiny (4-5 airframes), so no rate can be drawn. CONFIGURATION NOTES from the 1977 AOPA flight test (record, not accidents): narrow main-gear track from the inward-retracting gear, with sluggish ground steering that needs attention in crosswinds; weak yaw damping after rudder inputs; a T-tail stabilator that keeps flying below airplane flying speed, so a jerked pull on rollout pitches the nose up; and from a held deep stall the airplane breaks sharply down and to the right. Normal stalls were benign, with wings rolling level in accelerated stalls. INFERENCE: the 1983 accident (brakes failed during a turn, then excursion) loosely fits the narrow-track and steering comments, but the NTSB cited the brake seal and the pilot's decision, not the design.
notable: 1983-03-31 - Tomball TX (Hooks DWH) - N51AG, Anderson Greenwood 51 s/n 0001 (prototype; 1,520 h airframe time) - 0 injured, substantial damage - during taxi the nose-gear steering was insufficient for a left turn and the left brake had no fluid (deteriorated master-cylinder O-ring); the aircraft went onto soft ground and the left main gear collapsed when power was applied; cause: pilot planning/decision - NTSB FTW83LA173 - https://data.ntsb.gov/carol-repgen/api/Aviation/ReportMain/GenerateNewestReport/20852/pdf

why_died_detail: Record: the Aries was designed by Marvin Greenwood at Anderson, Greenwood & Co. (Houston valve maker): TC application Dec 1973, first flight 19 Jul 1973 per Wikipedia, TC 28 Jul 1976, about $1.2M spent on development and certification in FY1975-76 (AOPA 1977). Production was meant to go to Bellanca at Alexandria MN, which A-G was managing and taking a majority stake in. In winter 1976-77 the Viking plant was virtually shut down for lack of money, and A-G still had to raise capital before production could start (AOPA 1977). Target rate 12-14 per year; price expected $60-70k basic IFR (AOPA 1977). Bellanca went into receivership/bankruptcy in 1980 (Plane & Pilot 2010 and 2024). Plane & Pilot 2024 blames costs of the composite Skyrocket II program, estimated at $20-25M. Only s/n 0003-0005 (registered as 1980 builds) plus the prototype were completed; the injected Model 51A was approved in June 1980, too late. An ex-Bellanca president's recollection (archived 2004 owner page) says the 250 out-performed a 210, Bonanza and Viking in a fly-off, but he personally found it very ugly and the panel too high to see over. INFERENCE: it died of the parent company's finances, not a technical or safety failure. A revival would not inherit a safety problem but would face: carbureted 1960s O-540 power; 76 gal fuel giving ~860 nm at 75% (meeting 1,000 nm needs economy power); dated looks; narrow-track gear and yaw damping to improve.
rights_hints: TCDS A11SW (FAA DRS, Rev 2, 1 Jul 1980, status Current): Type Certificate Holder 'Anderson, Greenwood and Company' of Houston, Texas; former holder listed as 'Bellanca'; Production Certificate 1GL (Bellanca Aircraft Corp., Alexandria MN) for s/n 3 and up. So the TC was never transferred out of Anderson Greenwood. Secondary company histories (not verified by us; e.g. https://orbitcodex.com/organizations/anderson-greenwood-crosby) say Anderson Greenwood went to Keystone International (1986), Tyco (1997), Pentair (2012) and Emerson (2016-17), where it remains a valve brand. If so, Emerson or a successor may hold TC A11SW as an unused asset. This has to be checked with the FAA (Chicago/Fort Worth ACO) by the owner; we made no contact. Two of the four registered airframes (N77CT and N251AG, the prototype) are registered to the same private owner in Beaumont TX (registry). Owner-run site: https://consumleg.wixsite.com/bellancaaries250 . DRS search note: the Aries is filed under model '51', not 'T-250'; Model/Keyword searches for T-250/Aries return nothing relevant.
